name: Pancharama Kshetras
theme: Five Shiva temples of coastal Andhra born from a single shattered lingam
description: Tradition holds that when Kumara Swamy slew the asura Tarakasura, the Amrita lingam the demon wore at his throat would not die with him — so it was split into five pieces, and wherever a piece fell on the fertile deltas of coastal Andhra, a temple rose to guard it. These are the Pancharama Kshetras: Amararama at Amaravati, where Indra himself is said to have worshipped a marble lingam so tall that priests anoint it from an upper storey; Draksharama, the Kashi of the south, where sanctity doubles as a Shakti Peetha; Kumararama at Samalkota, installed by the warrior god himself; Ksheerarama at Palakollu, whose milk-white lingam rose where an arrow drew a stream of milk from the earth; and Somarama at Bhimavaram, whose lingam is said to change hue with the phases of the moon that installed it. Strung between the Krishna and Godavari deltas, the five make an easy few days' pilgrimage through rice country and river towns — Eastern Chalukya architecture, Telugu literary memory, and one shared story told five ways.
